Thank you, Madam Chair. Good morning, everybody. My name is Angela Crook, integrity commissioner for the City of Saskatoon. It is my pleasure to present to the Governor and some priorities committee today. The annual report of the Integrity Commissioner covering the 2023 calendar year.
There are several functions covered by the rule of the Integrity Commissioner. In 2023 there were two areas that I was called upon to perform advisory services and complaints.

The advisory function performed by the Integrity Commissioner involves responding to members of Council on questions of compliance with the Code of Ethics. In 2023 I received one request to provide an advance ruling from a member of Council and no request for general advice.
Written advanced rulings are more formal than a request for advice and a written advance ruling can be relied upon by the member in the event that there is a subsequent complaint.
Request for advice or more general in nature and cannot be relied upon by the member if a subsequent complaint is made that relates to the same conduct of the member.

The complaints can be categorized as formal and as informal. Formal complaints are requested a request that an investigation be performed into the conduct of a member of Council and they must comply with the criteria in the code.

I received three formal complaints in 2023. One of the formal complaints was withdrawn by the complainant. One of them was not investigated because it related to conduct that was not regulated by the Code of Ethics.
One complaint was investigated but the investigation was not complete when the annual report was issued and therefore will be reported in the 2024 annual report.

In formal complaints or inquiries are concerns of some sort that are raised by people. Sometimes the informal complaints are related to conduct covered by the Code of Ethics and sometimes they are entirely unrelated.
Either way I respond to each and every informal complaint or inquiry that is made to my office.
Most times it's just simply advising and guiding on what the role of the Integrity Commissioners office can be.

In 2023 I received six informal complaints. Four of the six informal complaints related to the conduct of a member of Council and two of them were not related to conduct that was regulated by the Code of Ethics.
Two main themes appear to me from the discussions I have been having with people through the complaint process over the last year.
There was some unhappiness with certain members of Council taking too long to respond to their concerns or never responding at all.
And the second was there were also some concerns related to a lack of respectful communication by some Council members.
These are just general observations though and they do not apply to each and every member of Council.
Respect is a common theme that comes up repeatedly in my work as integrity commissioner for the cities of Saskatoon and Regina and I see it coming up a lot in other jurisdictions as well.

My unscientific opinion from what I see in Saskatchewan and in other provinces is that the respect section of the Code of Ethics is one of the most common sections quoted in ethics complaints against Council members.
If opinions and debates are directed at the issues and the topics rather than the people who are communicating them.
Council members will be able to engage in meaningful debate and discussion without veering outside the boundaries of the Code of Ethics.
Looking forward for just a moment 2024 being an election year.
I will take this opportunity to remind all members of Council that the Code of Ethical Conduct by law has obligations imposed on a member of Council during the campaign period in an election year.
I would encourage everyone to read through that in detail to become familiar with those obligations.

The Code of Ethics by law does continue to apply during an election campaign but any complaints that I receive after August 1st this year will not be investigated until after the first meeting of Council.
In closing I would like to thank everyone in administration members of Council on the members of the public that I have worked with over the last year.
Everyone has been very cooperative and easy to work with which makes the investigation process much more efficient and effective.

Enhancing civic engagement advocating for flexible proclamation policies.
My name is Julie Adamsson from the friends of the Saskatoon out for station areas.
Deputy Mayor Beb Dubo chair members of the governance and priorities committee.
esteemed citizens and distinguished guests.
I stand before you today to advocate for a fundamental shift in our city's proclamation policies.
While well-intentioned inadvertently restricts the avenues of civic engagement by limiting organizations to only one.
Proclamation request per calendar year I propose that we we consider the reconstruction and adopt a more inclusive approach.
Allowing multiple proclamation requests within a single year or simply removing the restriction of one request per year.
Understanding proclamation.
Proclamation service ceremonial documents signed by the mayor carrying messages of significance interest or benefit to a considerable portion of our city's populace.
There are not mere endorsements but rather acknowledgments of the contributions made brain-to-victuals and organizations to the betterment of our community.
However the current policy limits the potential for recognizing diverse efforts and achievements within our city.
Principles of inclusivity and free expression.
Challenges of the current policy.
While policy 01028 was established to provide a standardized framework for considering proclamation requests.
This restrictive nature inadvertently haphors our ability to fully recognize the myriad contributions made by diverse organizations throughout the year.
The limitation of one proclamation per organization per year stifles innovation creativity and this spirit of community involvement benefits of flexible proclamation policies.
By embracing a more flexible approach to proclamation requests we cannot allow numerous benefits for our city.
Firstly it allows for a more comprehensive recognition of the multi-paceted efforts by various groups thereby fostering a stronger sense of community pride and engagement.
Secondly it encourages ongoing collaboration and partnership between the city and its stakeholders.
Promoting a culture of inclusivity and shared responsibility for community development.
Finally it enhances the visibility of our city's diverse tapestry of initiatives and achievements both locally and beyond.
Responsive community needs societal issues and community events are dynamic often necessitating timely recognition on support.
A rigid policy the limits proclamation requests can overlook emerging issues or significant events that weren't acknowledgement.
Plotability in the policy allows the city to respond promptly to community needs and demonstrate solidarity during times of significance.

Free expression and association upholding the right to free expression and association as enshrined in the human rights code entails providing equal opportunities for civic participation and recognition.
A flexible proclamation policy upholds those rights by ensuring that all voices are heard and valued.

A call to action. In light of the aforementioned considerations I urge the esteem members of this committee to reconsider policy 0108 and amend it to allow for multiple proclamation requests or simply remove the restriction of only one per year.
By doing so we affirm our commitment by fostering a vibrant inclusive and participatory community to celebrate the contributions of all its members.
In conclusion the current proclamation policy all rooted in noble intentions inadvertently constrains our ability to fully embrace the diversity and dynamism of our city.
By adopting a more flexible approach we can amplify the voices of our community stakeholders enhance civic engagement and uphold the principles of inclusivity and free expression.
Let us seize this opportunity to redefine our proclamation policies and chart a course towards a more vibrant and inclusive future for our city.
